label: Appearance
value: Anne is a tall girl.
unit: Anne is a tall, slender girl with a pale, freckled, pointed face, large expressive eyes that vary between green and gray, and a broad forehead. Her most distinctive feature is her thick hair, which is famously red—a lifelong source of grief to her—though it darkens to a rich auburn as she matures. At one point, her hair is accidentally dyed a bronze-green and must be shaved short.

label: Personality
value: Anne is an intensely imaginative girl.
unit: Anne is an intensely imaginative, emotional, and talkative girl who views the world with romantic wonder and deep passion. She possesses a dramatic flair, often using grand language to express her feelings, and alternates between ecstatic joys and the 'depths of despair.' Though fiercely quick-tempered when her looks—especially her hair—are criticized, she is deeply affectionate, loyal, and quick to repent when she realizes she has done wrong. Highly ambitious and hardworking, she matures into a thoughtful, bright, and determined young woman.

label: History
value: Anne Shirley arrives at Bright River station.
unit: Anne Shirley arrives at Bright River station expecting to be adopted by Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert, only to discover they had requested a boy to help on their farm. Though Marilla initially intends to send her back, Matthew is charmed by Anne's vivid chatter, and Marilla ultimately decides to keep her at Green Gables. Anne quickly settles into Avonlea, forming a passionate 'bosom friendship' with Diana Barry. Her early years are marked by dramatic misadventures: she flies into a rage at Mrs. Rachel Lynde for insulting her hair, mistakenly intoxicates Diana with currant wine, smashes a slate over Gilbert Blythe's head for calling her 'Carrots,' and breaks her ankle attempting a dare on a roof. Later, Anne saves Diana's baby sister from croup, earns the forgiveness of Diana's mother, and accidentally dyes her own hair green, necessitating a short haircut. At school, she enters a fierce academic rivalry with Gilbert Blythe. She enters Queen's Academy, ties with Gilbert for first place on the entrance exams, wins the prestigious Avery Scholarship, and completes her First Class teacher's license in one year. Following the sudden death of Matthew Cuthbert from heart failure and Marilla's failing eyesight, Anne selflessly gives up her college scholarship to remain at Green Gables and teach at the Avonlea school. She finally forgives Gilbert Blythe, ending their long-standing feud to become close friends.

label: History
value: Diana Barry is the daughter of Mr.
unit: Diana Barry grows up as the daughter of Mr. and Mrs. George Barry at Orchard Slope in Avonlea. In June, Matthew Cuthbert mentions her to Anne Shirley, noting her age and beauty. After returning from a visit to her aunt at Carmody, Diana meets Anne for the first time in the Orchard Slope garden and the two girls solemnly swear an oath of eternal bosom friendship over a imaginary running stream. They build a playhouse called 'Idlewild' in Mr. William Bell's birch grove and share many imaginative adventures. In October, Diana visits Green Gables for tea, where Anne accidentally serves her homemade currant wine instead of raspberry cordial. Unaware of what she is drinking, Diana consumes three tumblerfuls, becomes intoxicated and sick, and has to be helped home. Her strict mother, believing Anne intentionally got Diana drunk, forbids the girls from ever speaking or playing together again. They share a dramatic, tearful farewell by the Dryad's Bubble spring, exchanging locks of hair and vows of lifelong devotion. Diana secretly passes a note and a handmade tissue paper bookmarker to Anne in school to reassure her of her love. Months later, Diana's younger sister Minnie May contracts a severe case of croup while their parents are away at a political rally in Charlottetown.

They build a playhouse called 'Idlewild' in Mr. William Bell's birch grove and share many imaginative adventures. In October, Diana visits Green Gables for tea, where Anne accidentally serves her homemade currant wine instead of raspberry cordial. Unaware of what she is drinking, Diana consumes three tumblerfuls, becomes intoxicated and sick, and has to be helped home. Her strict mother, believing Anne intentionally got Diana drunk, forbids the girls from ever speaking or playing together again. They share a dramatic, tearful farewell by the Dryad's Bubble spring, exchanging locks of hair and vows of lifelong devotion. Diana secretly passes a note and a handmade tissue paper bookmarker to Anne in school to reassure her of her love. Months later, Diana's younger sister Minnie May contracts a severe case of croup while their parents are away at a political rally in Charlottetown.

label: History
value: Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea
unit: Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea after spending three years in Alberta with his sick father, falling behind in his school progression as a result. Upon his return to the Avonlea school, he quickly resumed his position at the top of his class. On his first day back, he attempted to get the attention of Anne Shirley by pulling her braid and calling her 'Carrots,' causing her to smash her slate over his head in anger. Although Gilbert publicly took the blame for the incident and apologized to Anne at the school door, she refused to forgive him. On a later occasion, when the master punished Anne by forcing her to sit with Gilbert, he tried to comfort her by offering her a candy heart, which she crushed under her shoe. Despite Anne's coldness and grudge against him, Gilbert maintained a good-natured academic rivalry with her throughout their time in the Fourth and Fifth classes. By the end of the term, he was promoted with her into the fifth class to study Latin, geometry, French, and algebra. After years of rivalry, Gilbert gave up his application for the Avonlea school so that Anne could teach there and stay with Marilla, opting instead to teach at White Sands. Upon learning of his sacrifice, Anne forgave him and they finally became close friends.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert lived an unmarred, quiet life at Green Gables.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived an unmarred, quiet life at Green Gables with her brother Matthew, managing their homestead. Wanting a young orphan boy to assist Matthew with farm work, they arranged through acquaintances to adopt one from Nova Scotia. Due to a misunderstanding, an eleven-year-old girl named Anne Shirley arrived instead. Though Marilla initially insisted on returning the orphan girl, she was moved by pity and Matthew's quiet persistence, agreeing to keep Anne and raise her properly. Over the next five years, Marilla navigated the challenges of raising an unusually imaginative, talkative, and impulsive girl. She strictly corrected Anne's outbursts, taught her prayers and catechism, and oversaw her schooling and home chores. Through various incidents—including Anne's temper explosion at Mrs. Rachel Lynde, her accidental intoxication of Diana Barry, the loss of Marilla's prized amethyst brooch, and Anne's green hair mishap—Marilla learned to temper her strictness with deep affection and a newfound sense of maternity. label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert decided with his sister Marilla to adopt a native-born orphan boy.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert, a lifelong resident of Green Gables in Avonlea, decided with his sister Marilla to adopt a native-born orphan boy to help with farm work as he grew older. He drove to Bright River station to collect the child, only to discover a mistake had been made and a young girl named Anne Shirley had been sent instead. Unable to leave her at the station, he brought her home and immediately grew fond of her talkative and imaginative nature. Though Marilla initially insisted on returning Anne, Matthew quietly advocated for keeping her, realizing they could be a good influence on the child. Throughout her upbringing, Matthew constantly indulged Anne, secretly buying her sweeties, defending her against harsh punishments, and encouraging her romantic spirit. When Anne wished for a fashionable dress with puffed sleeves, Matthew braved his intense shyness to purchase the materials and had Mrs. Lynde make it as a Christmas gift. He took great pride in Anne's academic achievements, encouraging her to study for the Entrance Examinations and eventually for Queen's Academy. Though he suffered from worsening heart trouble, he continued working the farm until he unexpectedly passed away from a sudden heart attack after reading news of the failure of the Abbey Bank.

Unable to leave her at the station, he brought her home and immediately grew fond of her talkative and imaginative nature. Though Marilla initially insisted on returning Anne, Matthew quietly advocated for keeping her, realizing they could be a good influence on the child. Throughout her upbringing, Matthew constantly indulged Anne, secretly buying her sweeties, defending her against harsh punishments, and encouraging her romantic spirit. When Anne wished for a fashionable dress with puffed sleeves, Matthew braved his intense shyness to purchase the materials and had Mrs. Lynde make it as a Christmas gift. He took great pride in Anne's academic achievements, encouraging her to study for the Entrance Examinations and eventually for Queen's Academy. Though he suffered from worsening heart trouble, he continued working the farm until he unexpectedly passed away from a sudden heart attack after reading news of the failure of the Abbey Bank.

label: History
value: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster of Avonlea school.
unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster of Avonlea school, where he notoriously paid more attention to his student Prissy Andrews than to his general teaching duties. During his tenure, he humiliated Anne Shirley by publicly shaming her temper after she broke a slate over Gilbert Blythe's head, and later punished her for tardiness by forcing her to sit next to Gilbert. Following this incident, Anne refused to attend school under his instruction for several weeks. At the end of the school term, Mr. Phillips delivered an affecting farewell speech to his pupils before leaving Avonlea, a departure that was facilitated by his uncle's influence on the school board.

unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster of Avonlea school, where he notoriously paid more attention to his student Prissy Andrews than to his general teaching duties. Following this incident, Anne refused to attend school under his instruction for several weeks. At the end of the school term, Mr. Phillips delivered an affecting farewell speech to his pupils before leaving Avonlea, a departure that was facilitated by his uncle's influence on the school board.

label: History
value: Priscilla Grant entered Queen's Academy in Charlottetown.
unit: Priscilla Grant entered Queen's Academy in Charlottetown to pursue a Second Class teacher's license. There she formed a close friendship with Anne Shirley, Stella Maynard, and Philippa Gordon, becoming part of their ambitious circle of students. During her time at Queen's, she joined a girls' story club where members wrote weekly stories under pseudonyms, though she insisted on keeping romance out of her own sensible tales. Upon finishing her course, she secured a school to teach for the following year.

value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived in Lynde's Hollow on the main road of Avonlea.
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived in Lynde's Hollow on the main road of Avonlea, keeping a sharp eye on all passers-by. Upon seeing Matthew Cuthbert unusually dressed up and driving out of Avonlea, her curiosity led her to visit Green Gables, where Marilla Cuthbert informed her of their intention to adopt an orphan boy. Mrs. Rachel voiced strong disapproval and pessimism regarding the decision, and later spread the news through the community. Weeks later, after recovering from a severe bout of grippe, she visited Green Gables to inspect the adopted orphan, Anne Shirley, but offended the child by calling her skinny, homely, freckled, and red-headed, provoking an angry outburst from Anne. Though initially indignant and advising a whipping, Mrs. Rachel readily accepted Anne's dramatic apology the following evening, forgave her, and offered her a bouquet of June lilies. Subsequently, Mrs. Rachel interacted frequently with the Cuthbert household, keeping track of Anne's doings at school and Sunday-school.

label: Personality
value: Miss Stacy is a teacher.
unit: Miss Stacy is a sympathetic, broadminded, and tactful teacher who possesses a gift for winning her pupils' affections. She is an inspiring educator who encourages students to think, explore, and discover independently rather than sticking strictly to beaten paths. She also holds high standards, urging her pupils to write simply and become their own severest critics.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy is hired as the new teacher for Avonlea school.
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy is hired as the new teacher for Avonlea school, becoming the community's first female teacher. She quickly earns the adoration of her pupils by introducing engaging activities such as physical culture exercises, field days for nature study, and Friday afternoon recitations and dialogues. In November, she organizes a student concert in the hall to raise money for a schoolhouse flag. She also organizes an advanced class for students intending to prepare for the Queen's Academy entrance examination, giving them extra lessons for an hour after school. Although offered a position in her home district's grade school at the end of the year, she chooses to remain in Avonlea to see her students through their entrance exams.
